findings.title: When the replies to the outward-action rule's blocks leave no assistant row in the record, the rule blocks at every stop without end (8 of 8 simulated stops), past the owner's 'twice at most'. The tree before this change let the stop go after one block, and the table cannot tell the shipped rule from one that ends the loop.
findings.component: hooks/turngate.py Model.feedback (line 2513) and f1_decision; receiptlaw.py decide (same count)
findings.rule_quoted: How often it blocks (the owner's answer: "Yes, twice at most"). At most twice in one stretch: again when its first block was not answered, then the stop is let go.  //  Q3 | Block again after an unanswered Stop block | "Yes, twice at most" | F1_MAX_BLOCKS = 2, PROMPT_CLASS_MAX_BLOCKS = 1

mut.py: MU01-retry-counts-every-block    == 950 cases: 950 pass, 0 fail ==
with all three rules missing (sim.py ... empty all): F1 8 blocks and the receipt gate 4 (its maximum is 1)
findings.expected: At most two F1 blocks (and one receipt or prompt-class block) in one stretch, whatever the record holds: the third stop is let go. feedback() now counts an unanswered block only when it is the record's LAST block. So with two unanswered blocks the earlier one is never counted again, own stays 1, and the retry shortcut no longer fires because the last block is counted. Counting every block on a retry (MU01) gives exactly two in all three modes and passes all 950 cases, so no case pins the choice.
findings.how_it_arises: It needs two blocked stops in a row with no assistant row between them in the record: an empty reply after the block, or a record that is more than one stop behind. The builder's own premise for AS-2 is that the record can lag, but only a one-stop lag is covered. Whether the program ever leaves no assistant row is not observed here, because the real record cannot be opened. Fixtures use the builder's real row shapes (feedback row, hook_blocking_error attachment, stop row with hookErrors). This is a regression: c3c8615 let the stop go after one block on the same record.

findings.title: A helper's outward act noted while the session is idle (after the completed stop row, before the owner's next message) is charged to no stretch, so an ungoverned turn's background helper can commit and push with no block at any stop.
findings.rule_quoted: the Stop gate counts the note as an outward action of the stretch ... it belongs to the stretch when it is later than the stretch's own first row (the owner's message or the stop it starts at) ... A helper's act is charged to the stretch in which it happens, also when the helper was started in an earlier turn
findings.observed:
MISMATCH L1    gate: allow     rule: block:F1   | helper commits while the session is idle (after the stop row, before the owner's next message): counted somewhere?
MISMATCH L1b   gate: allow     rule: block:F1   | same; the helper's completion notice arrives inside the owner's next turn
ok       L1c   gate: block:F1  rule: block:F1   | control: same note, the wake comes before any owner message
ok       L1d   gate: block:F1  rule: block:F1   | control: the note is stamped after the owner's 'thanks'
findings.expected: Some stop counts the commit, either the launching stretch or the next one. In fact the launching turn's stop passed before the helper acted (first round G04a). The next stretch starts at the owner's message, which is later than the note. So the act falls between the two stretches and is never judged. This gap is not listed among the helper limits (README:377-379).
findings.how_it_arises: An ungoverned turn starts a background helper (run_in_background) and stops. The helper commits and pushes while the session is idle, and the owner types a new message before the helper's completion notice wakes the session. Ledger notes use the real pre-tool hook format (R.ledger_line) and the records use the builder's real row shapes. The same gap existed at c3c8615, which placed notes against the row after the stretch start, so this is not a regression; the new placement rule just does not close it.

findings.title: Of 189 permission denials recorded in this repository's own results/ files, the denial leads recognise 10. A call denied in one of the other wordings and not flagged with toolDenialKind counts its and-chain's commit, so a turn that did nothing outward is blocked.
findings.rule_quoted: Not an action at all: ... a call that was denied or rejected  //  A call was denied when its result row carries toolDenialKind ..., or when its result is an error whose text STARTS ... with one of DENIAL_LEADS  //  A false block is a defect too
findings.repro_command: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=WORK2/fd-stop/tmp python3 -I WORK2/fd-stop/survey_denials.py | tail -3; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=WORK2/fd-stop/tmp python3 WORK2/fd-stop/bbx.py R1c R1k
findings.observed:
== 189 recorded denials in 108 files; 10 taken for a denial without the flag, 179 not
(leads not recognised include: 'This Bash command contains multiple operations. The following parts require approval: ...', 'Claude requested permissions to use ...', 'This command changes directory before running ...', 'Contains brace with quote character ...', "A variable in this command can't be checked ...", "ls in '<path>' was blocked. For security ..."; each recorded with tool_result_meta non_execution_kind 'user-rejected', e.g. fixed/results/2026-10-13/system-validation/raw/live/trig/after-report-7-2/out.jsonl, version 2.1.296)
MISMATCH R1c    gate: block:F1           rule: allow              | denied in a non-interactive run (headless wording), no flag: nothing ran
MISMATCH R1k    gate: block:F1           rule: allow              | denied: the wording recorded 2026-10-13 in this repo's results/ (no flag): nothing ran
ok       R1c2   gate: allow              rule: allow              | same with the flag
findings.expected: A denied call is not an action. The lead list exists for rows that lack the flag (the README keeps the 'older shape' leads on purpose). Yet it holds only one of the real non-interactive denial wordings ('This command requires approval') and none of the others. The field those recorded rows do carry (tool_result_meta / non_execution_kind) is not read.
findings.how_it_arises: A run where nobody can answer permission prompts (headless, or a scheduled run) and the record's row lacks toolDenialKind. A denied 'git add -A && git commit -m x && git push' drops only the push, so the commit counts and the stop is blocked up to twice. Not verified: whether current transcripts always carry toolDenialKind for these denials. The builder observed it only for a hook denial (version 2.1.325), and the recorded shapes are stream-json output rows, not transcript rows.

findings.title: The README states what HELPER_ACT_PLACED_BY_TIME = True costs but not what its alternative costs: with False, a background helper started by an ungoverned turn commits and pushes without any stop counting it.
findings.rule_quoted: Its cost: the owner's next turn ("thanks") can be blocked once for a background helper's late commit, and loading the governors answers it. False: such an act is charged only to a stretch whose main thread started a helper (`HELPER_TOOLS`) before it.

findings.expected: The owner is offered False as a one-click overrule (decisions.md:37-40). The statement should say that False drops such acts entirely, because the launching turn's stop has already passed, not only that it moves them. Neither value implements the first round's rule as given (charge the act to the launching turn).
findings.how_it_arises: Only if the owner flips the default on the strength of this paragraph. Fixtures: the first round's ledger.py (the real pre-tool hook writes the note) and the builder's row shapes.

findings.title: The False value of PROMPT_CLASS_SILENT_WITHOUT_OWNER_MESSAGE does more than stated: a denied write counts as 'a real write', and a scheduled run in a record that does hold an owner message is judged too. No case exercises either False path, and four breaks of that path survive the table.
findings.rule_quoted: when the record holds no owner message (`PROMPT_CLASS_SILENT_WITHOUT_OWNER_MESSAGE = True`, a default; False: such a stretch that made a real write is judged as work that needs plan-gate)
findings.repro_command: cd WORK2/fd-stop && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=WORK2/fd-stop/tmp PCVALUE=False HOOKS=WORK2/fd-stop/h-pcF python3 WORK2/fd-stop/pccases.py

MISMATCH P7  gate: block:prompt-class rule: allow              | no owner message, the one write was DENIED: no real write happened
note     P4  gate: block:prompt-class rule: ?                  | scheduled run in a record that DOES hold an owner message (earlier turn), a write
ok       P1  gate: block:prompt-class rule: block:prompt-class | file starts at a compaction (no owner message), a real write, no governor
mut.py: MU10-wrote-sidechain, MU11-wrote-any-row, MU12-write-class, MU09-helperF-window: each == 950 cases: 950 pass, 0 fail ==
findings.expected: With False, the rule judges only a stretch that made a real write (a call that ran), and only where the record holds no owner message, as the name and the README say. Each value of a switch the owner may click has a case.
findings.how_it_arises: Only with the switch set to False. wrote() reads the tool calls (model.uses) without their results, so a denied Write counts. The test is gov_kind != 'owner', which is also true for every scheduled run.

notes: Regression list: AS-1, AS-5, AS-6, AS-7 and AS-8 are fixed. AS-2 is fixed for the shape reported. AS-3 and AS-4 are left open on purpose and stated plainly. The builder's evidence (replay totals, AS breaks, the U cases) re-ran as claimed. The new counting rule (the record's last block counts on a retry) fixes the reported one-stop lag. But when replies leave no row, it trades the old under-block for an unbounded loop (DS-1). Counting every block on a retry (MU01) fixes both and passes the whole table. Fixture realism: every record uses the builder's selftest_rows shapes; DS-3 uses denial wordings recorded in the repo's own results/. Report saved at WORK2/fd-stop/findings.json. MORE: Model.merges_made uses the same was_denied, so a merge denied in an unrecognised wording counts as an earlier merge for rule C. That fails closed and costs one card more; not run. MORE: MU13 ($TMPDIR/$OTHER taken for scratch) survives the table; it affects the advisory only (low). MORE: the commit message says 'there is no third' block; DS-1 shows a third block and more in the no-row case.
